Research
at NTU

Four projects at CMLAB form one coherent pipeline: reasoning about 3D space, labeling 3D assets, generating scenes from language, and rendering them photorealistically — the foundations of an embodied-AI research program.

SpatioRoute — Dynamic Prompt Routing for Zero-Shot Spatial Reasoning 2nd Workshop on 3D-LLM/VLA · CVPR 2026 · Presented in Denver, USA · arXiv:2605.18209
Presented in person — SpatioRoute poster session · 2nd Workshop on 3D-LLM/VLA · CVPR 2026 · Denver, Colorado, USA · June 2026
+5%
Accuracy over fixed-prompt baselines on SQA3D
0
Fine-tuning · 3D sensors · point-cloud inputs required
2
Routing modes — rule-based (R) and LLM-driven (L)

Spatial question answering over egocentric video asks vision-language models to reason about 3D positions, scene affordances, and directional relationships — zero-shot, with no task-specific training. Existing pipelines apply one fixed prompt to every question. SpatioRoute replaces it with a router: each question is mapped to a semantically tailored prompt before VLM inference — SpatioRoute-R deterministically maps SQA3D question typologies to specialized templates; SpatioRoute-L uses a small text LLM with few-shot demonstrations, video-free at routing time.

Question-aware routing beats uniform reasoning: uniform Chain-of-Thought prompting can degrade spatial VQA on Qwen-family VLMs.

Across multiple VLM families on SQA3D, SpatioRoute improves accuracy by up to 5% — a strong state of the art for zero-shot, video-only spatial VQA without 3D point-cloud input. The insight that when and how a model reasons should adapt to the question carries directly into my study plan on reasoning for robotics.

Co-authors: G. J. Faure · H.-T. Su · W. H. Hsu Paper Project page Code

Project / 02

Auto Labeling & Captioning for 3D Objects

Embodied Scene Generation · 01
Qwen2.5-VL · Objaverse · ABO

Objaverse and ABO meshes ship with thin product text — not enough for language-driven retrieval and placement. This pipeline turns raw meshes into a retrieval-ready object library: six axis-aligned multi-view renders per mesh, structured VLM captioning, semantic orientation (front / up axes with confidence), placement affordances (wall-side vs. open-space vs. floor), and physical attributes — metric size, weight, material. All merged into a unified object database (SQLite + JSONL) behind a human-verification UI — the asset foundation every downstream scene is built on. Project page Code

Labeling UI — semantic front / up axes, six cube views, VLM caption & metric physical attributes for placement
Project / 03

Text-to-Scene Generation from a 3D Object Library

Embodied Scene Generation · 02
Three.js CAD · MCP / REST agent tools

On top of the labeled library sits a browser CAD for indoor architecture and a text-to-scene agent: a planner extracts furniture, placements, and spatial relations from natural language; a caption-aware retriever selects matching meshes; a composer solves poses and emits Scene JSON for the CAD editor. Sparse prompts like “bedroom” expand through room presets; rich spatial language is followed directly. An incremental edit API — “add a table at the corner” — modifies an existing scene without regenerating walls or prior furniture, and the whole system is exposed as MCP / REST tools for LLM-agent workflows. Project page Code

Browser CAD — incremental edit on a generated scene: object library, 2D/3D plan, live Scene JSON & MCP-ready API (demo frame)
Research Dossier01 · Research at NTU03
01 · Research at NTU — continued
Project / 04

Reflective Mesh Compositing in 3DGS Scenes

Hybrid rendering · WebGL
SuperSplat extension · Live demo

This system combines two rendering paradigms in a single scene: the 3DGS environment is drawn by splat rasterization, while reflections on mesh objects are computed by ray operations — screen-space ray marching against a combined splat + mesh depth buffer, with reflection probes capturing the splat world as prefiltered cubemaps for 360° fallback. A confidence-weighted blend unifies both, so a glossy GLB object sits inside the splat scene and reflects it — something neither pipeline can do alone, since splats produce no triangles or G-buffer for standard reflection APIs. Runs in the browser at interactive rates (~62 fps, 120k-polygon car on a laptop GPU), extending the open-source SuperSplat viewer — a key building block toward photorealistic robot simulation.

Project page Live demo Video Code

One scene, two paradigms — the 3D Gaussian scene is rasterized as splats while the mesh object's reflections are computed by ray operations (SSR ray marching + reflection probes), unified in a single WebGL canvas.

02 · Study Plan

Study Plan

Research vision

Close the loop between 3D scene generation, robot learning, and reasoning: automatically generate diverse, physically plausible, photorealistic environments and long-horizon tasks in which robots learn by imitation — and give robots the reasoning to plan and check their own actions inside them. The unifying paradigm is generate-and-validate: generative models propose scenes, tasks, and plans; validation modules — spatial reasoning, physics checks, VLM critics — verify them.

Phase 1
Completed / Ongoing

Foundations — assets, generation & spatial reasoning

SpatioRoute (CVPR 2026 Workshop), the labeled 3D object library, text-to-scene generation, and hybrid 3DGS–mesh rendering: the assets, tools, and reasoning baselines for everything that follows.

Delivered · Section 01
Phase 2
Year 1–2

Simulation-ready scene & task generation

Extend text-to-scene from static layouts to simulation-ready environments — physics-consistent placement, articulated and interactable objects, photorealistic 3DGS-hybrid appearance. On top: long-horizon task generation — multi-step tasks with goal specifications, subgoal decompositions, and programmatic success criteria grounded in the generated scene.

Target: CVPR / ICCV / ICRA
Phase 3
Year 2–3

Robot learning in generated environments

Use generated scene–task pairs as a data engine for policy learning via imitation learning, synthesizing demonstrations in simulation and studying how generator-driven scene and task diversity affects policy robustness and generalization.

Target: CoRL / ICRA / RSS
Phase 4
Year 3–4

Reasoning for robotics — generative planning with validation

VLM/LLM planners generate action plans for long-horizon tasks; validators check spatial feasibility, physical plausibility, and task progress before and during execution — extending the SpatioRoute insight that adaptive reasoning beats uniform reasoning into embodied action: when should a robot think, and when should it act?

Target: CVPR / CoRL / Journal
Phase 5
Year 4

Integration & dissertation

Unify generation → learning → reasoning → validation into one benchmarked system; complete the dissertation.

02 · Study Plan — Research Problems & Positioning

The Open Problem: Task-Aware Worlds
for Long-Horizon Robot Learning

The field faces a dilemma. Manual benchmarks like BEHAVIOR-1K offer verifiable long-horizon activities — but only 50 fixed, hand-built scenes. Generative systems like RoboGen scale to open vocabulary — but produce short-horizon skills with ad-hoc, unverifiable goals. No existing system generates scenes that are simultaneously task-aware, long-horizon, physically validated, and programmatically checkable. Closing this gap is the central objective of my doctoral research.

Input — text + reference image
“Create a scene for a long-horizon task: the robot collects the trash in the kitchen and throws it outside the house.”
→
Generative
Model
→
Output — validated scene–task pair
Scene with every affordance the task requires — trash can, door, outdoor bins — in a physics-consistent layout.
Task: clean the trash · Sub-tasks: 1 Go to the kitchen → 2 Pick up the trash bag → 3 Go out of the house → 4 Put it in front of the house
READY TO USE IN SIMULATOR
Concept — joint scene–task generation: the task specification drives which objects, articulations and rooms must exist
Problem / 01

Task-aware scene generation

Current generators build scenes first and hope tasks fit. A long-horizon task defines its own requirements — “throw out the trash” needs a trash can, a traversable door, an outdoor destination. Scene and task must be generated jointly, so every required affordance provably exists.

Problem / 02

Verifiable goal specification

RoboGen-style LLM goals are ad hoc: success cannot be checked programmatically. BDDL shows the alternative — predicate-logic goals with initial and goal conditions. Generated tasks must ship with machine-checkable goals, or training signal cannot be trusted at scale.

Problem / 03

Long-horizon structure & semantic state

Multi-step tasks span rooms and need articulated objects (doors, drawers) plus semantic states — open/closed, inside/on-top. Generated scenes today are mostly static single-room layouts; long-horizon learning demands stateful, interactable worlds.

Problem / 04

Validation — physics, edits & policies

Visually plausible is not physically usable: interpenetration, unstable support, and unreachable placements silently corrupt training data. Scenes must pass physics validation, stay editable for curricula, and ultimately be validated by the policies trained in them.

Core methodology — the generate-and-validate loop; only validated scene–task pairs enter the training set, and policy results steer future generation
M1

Joint scene–task generation (→ Problems 01, 03)

Extend my text-to-scene planner to be task-conditioned: the task specification is compiled into a required-affordance list (objects, articulations, rooms, connectivity), the retriever draws matching assets from my labeled object database, and the composer solves a layout in which every required affordance provably exists and is reachable — across multiple rooms for long-horizon tasks.

M2

Goal compiler with programmatic checkers (→ Problem 02)

Compile each generated task into BDDL-like predicate goals — initial conditions, goal conditions, and sub-goal decomposition over the scene graph (inside/on-top, open/closed) — with a success checker that runs in the simulator. Every task ships with its own machine-checkable definition, so training signal quality does not depend on an LLM's judgment.

M3

Three-stage validation stack (→ Problem 04)

Stage 1 — physics: collision, support stability, and reachability checks in simulation. Stage 2 — semantic: VLM critics and SpatioRoute-style spatial reasoning verify that the scene affords the task. Stage 3 — policy-in-the-loop: imitation-learned policies are the final validator; per-scene success statistics feed back to steer generation and build curricula via my incremental-edit API.

Evaluation protocol
  • Generation quality: scene validity rate (physics checks passed), task solvability rate (oracle planner can complete), and goal-checker precision against human judgment.
  • Learning value: success rate of imitation-learned policies on held-out generated tasks and on BEHAVIOR-style manual tasks — trained on my generated data vs. RoboGen-style and fixed-scene baselines.
  • Scaling: policy performance as a function of generated scene/task diversity — the data-engine claim, tested directly.
Risks & mitigation
  • Articulated asset quality: generation of articulated objects may lag — mitigate with curated articulated datasets (e.g., PartNet-Mobility-style assets) merged into my labeled library.
  • Goal-compilation errors: LLM compilation can be wrong — mitigate with rule-based verification of predicates plus human spot-checks on samples.
  • Scope of semantic states: full BEHAVIOR-level state coverage is infeasible for one PhD — deliberately target a tractable subset (open/closed, inside/on-top, at-location) that already unlocks long-horizon tasks.
Feasibility rests on delivered work, not promises: the labeled object library, the text-to-scene system with its edit API, the 3DGS hybrid renderer, and a CVPR 2026 workshop publication already exist — built at NTU CMLAB under Prof. Winston H. Hsu, with the lab's GPU infrastructure and an active embodied-AI research group. This scholarship funds the step from infrastructure to science.
